historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly identifies the physical/destructive split but does not prove utility provenance, image authenticity, de-energized jumper handling, write verification or the full restored-jumper BMC state.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly keeps the concrete operator path out of BLOCKED and adds critical gates, but the suggested `-P` post-check exposes credentials and firmware revision alone is incomplete acceptance.
historical_reviews.related_cases: This is an AST2600 debug-ROM recovery/programming path, distinct from normal update service or U-Boot TFTP flashing because the boot strap/jumper and host-side UART programmer select a low-level SPI target.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Bind the host utility, signed encrypted image, fixture wiring, jumper positions and SPI target to an approved procedure; change straps only de-energized, capture write/verify output and prove normal boot after restoring the production strap.

original_test_intent: Demonstrate that the approved encrypted AST2600 BMC ROM can be programmed through the debug UART path with the required boot strap, after which the production jumper state is restored and the BMC returns on the intended firmware with normal management functions.
original_method: Identify the exact board/BMC/SPI target and debug/recovery jumper positions; verify the trusted host utility and signed encrypted image; back up required firmware/configuration and prepare external recovery; remove AC and confirm de-energization before changing the strap; connect the mapped UART/COM port, apply stable AC and let a qualified operator run the source command once; require terminal write/verify success; remove AC, restore the production jumper, reapply power and verify firmware, boot mode, services, network/configuration, sensors, inventory and logs.
manual_activity: A qualified operator de-energizes the board, changes/restores the approved debug jumper, connects the mapped UART, controls AC and runs the trusted local programmer; the agent may validate artifacts/transcript and collect secure post-flash OOB evidence.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Execute one identity-bound AST2600 debug-port programming transaction under operator control, prove terminal write/verify success, restore the production strap de-energized and validate full BMC recovery.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds tool/image provenance, electrical/fixture identity, de-energized jumper interlock, backup/recovery, no-retry semantics, secure credentials and full normal-strap health evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A utility success line or firmware revision alone cannot prove the correct SPI was programmed, the normal strap was restored, the intended image activated or BMC configuration/services survived.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A wrong strap, voltage, COM mapping, SPI/CS target, incompatible encrypted image or interrupted write can leave the BMC unbootable and may require an external programmer.

review_improvement: Retains the exact AST2600 debug-port mechanism while binding every destructive target and physical strap transition to an approved fixture and recovery contract, followed by normal-strap functional proof.
independent_technical_reasoning: The debug jumper determines an early boot/programming path, so its position and the AC transition are functional inputs, not incidental setup. The host utility's `--spi 0 --cs 0` selects a physical flash and the encrypted image must match both the silicon security state and board layout. A successful UART transfer can still target the wrong chip or leave the board in recovery strap mode. Consequently acceptance requires de-energized strap control, immutable utility/image/target identity, write verification, production-strap restoration and normal BMC service/configuration evidence with an external recovery path retained.
